title: Write app/robots.ts and app/sitemap.ts for zedu-fe, tested on a local build
description: First task of this approach. In zedu-fe cybertron-integration, add src/app/robots.ts (allow marketing routes, disallow /auth/, /billing/ and the invitation routes, point to the sitemap) and src/app/sitemap.ts listing every public page under src/app/(homepage) (static pages plus the contributor pages). Deliver: the full diff, the output of a local production build (next build, then next start) showing /robots.txt returns text/plain and /sitemap.xml returns valid application/xml (paste the curl output and the XML), and the curl re-check for production after deploy. Every page in the sitemap must return 200 locally. Do not push or deploy; the diff is handed to the team.

goal.title: Publish a real robots.txt and sitemap.xml for zedu.chat, by Fri 6 Nov
goal.description:
Checked on 22 Oct 2026: zedu.chat/robots.txt and zedu.chat/sitemap.xml both return 200 with the website's HTML page (about 22 KB, content type text/html), not a robots file or a sitemap. Search engines get no crawl rules and no list of pages.

Success looks like: robots.txt returns plain text that allows the public marketing pages, blocks the signed-in app paths and points to the sitemap; sitemap.xml returns valid XML that lists every public marketing page once, with the address that page's canonical tag uses; both are checked with curl (status 200, correct content type) and the sitemap is submitted in Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools. Note what was and wasn't checked.

workstream.title: Add app/robots.ts and app/sitemap.ts so Next.js serves real files before the [org] route catches them
workstream.description: Cause, from zedu-fe cybertron-integration (17 Oct 2026): src/app has no robots.ts or sitemap.ts, so /robots.txt falls into the (client)/[org] dynamic route and is treated as an organisation slug (the live HTML for /robots.txt shows params {org: 'robots.txt'}). Next.js's built-in metadata files fix this at the source. Tasks: (1) add src/app/robots.ts allowing the marketing routes, disallowing the signed-in app paths and pointing to the sitemap; (2) add src/app/sitemap.ts listing every public (homepage) route, with contributor and resource pages generated from the same data the pages use; (3) after deploy, curl both to confirm text/plain and application/xml, validate the sitemap, and submit it in Search Console and Bing.
